newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch dealers play down options expiry impact.
newsitem.headline: Dutch dealers play down options expiry impact.

text.p: Share and option dealers said on Wednesday many open contracts on Amsterdam's options bourse would be extended ahead of Friday's expiry and they did not expect a big impact from option contracts that are expiring.
"Many contracts will be extended," said one dealer.
Another dealer said a sudden change in market sentiment could disrupt the market in combination with the expiry, adding that this was not very likely in the short term.
"There could be a problem if there is an intervention involving the dollar," he said, but he did not expect this in the very short term.

Dealers said nervousness among some players in the market ahead of Friday's expiry was overdone, despite a press release from the Amsterdam Exchanges saying it has to take account of the possibility of unprecedented turnover this week caused by the July expiration.

The AEX-Optionbourse said it had based its expectation on the number of July options in-the-money, which by Monday's close had risen to 850,000 contracts. It added a large number of these would be closed or rolled over before or during the last trading day for the July series.
In-the-money contracts offer more advantageous exercise prices than the market prices of the underlying stock.
"Many players will roll over their current in-the-money contracts into an at-the-money call contract with a settlement date later this year," said one dealer.
The Option bourse said the busiest expiration day so far was in January when the number of contracts in-the-money was 380,000 and the number of contracts settled during the expiration was 411,000.
Dealers said most business in the options market was in ABN AMRO options and options covering the AEX share index.
The AEX Optionbeurs decided last week to postpone the introduction of new options series and to reduce the number of new series, anticipating a hectic situation.

"The AEX optionbourse can decide to close the day's trading prematurely if, during the trading day before Friday's expiration, excessive volume causes the backlock in the daily processing of transactions to become so great as to endanger timely settlement," it said.
"If things get extremely busy during the coming week it can also be decided not to allow any extended trading period," it added.
